newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Stan Chart hit by broker downgrades.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Stan Chart hit by broker downgrades.

text.p: Shares in Standard Chartered Plc fell on Wednesday as two brokerages seperately reduced earnings forecasts for the Anglo-Asian banking group following briefings with executives from the company.
The shares were down 11p at 931-1/2p by 1152 GMT in volume of 1.9 million shares, after earlier dropping as much as 30-1/2p.
Mark Thomas, banking analyst at Collins Stewart, cut his pre-tax profit forecast for 1997 to 880 million stg from 920 million stg and changed his recommendation to a "sell" from a "hold".
Market sources said analysts at SBC Warburg had also reduced their earnings forecasts, though Warburg banking analyst Chris Ellerton declined comment.
Thomas listed the strength of sterling, slower-than-expected recovery of bad debts and the prospect of tougher regulation of the mortgage lending market in Hong Kong as reasons for the downgrade.
Standard's analyst briefings were a regular round of meetings as the company approaches its "closed" season on June 20 ahead of first-half results on August 6.
A spokesman for the bank said analysts seemed to be concentrating on the effect of sterling's strength would have on profits, but declined further comment.
Standard's share price has risen sharply since the beginning of the year, with investors lured by the growth prospects of its Asian network together with lingering bid hopes.

Up 53 percent at a record 10.45 stg by May 9 from its year's low of 680p set early January, it has even outperformed the bouyant bank sector in the last six weeks, which has been boosted by the Halifax and Alliance & Leicester flotations.

In an interview with Reuters in April, the banks's chief executive Malcolm Williamson said Standard expected to expand dramatically across Asia over the next few years. The region accounted for about 70 per cent of Standard's 870 million stg pre-tax profits in 1996.
Wlliamson said the bank already had large businesses in Hong Kong, Sinagapore and Malaysia and highlighted the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand as possible areas to expand in.
Standard remained upbeat about prospects in Hong Kong and Williamson has said the bank is looking to continue to develop its business in the territory and in China.

The bank has formed joint ventures in Asia in the last year with Westpac banking Corp, First Chicago NBD Corp and Fleet Financial Services which it hoped would entrench its dominant position as a leading player in the region.
Standard said in April it had had discussions about further alliances in Asia with more than five European banks and hoped to make an announcement in coming months.
